text:
alex_m: Hey team — noticed a new garnishment on my last paystub for $420. I moved from OR to WA last month, but this looks like a state/county levy? Also my 401(k) deferral dropped from 10% to 4% this check. Can someone help?

people_ops: Sorry to see that @alex_m. Can you DM a screenshot of the paystub (black out SSN) and confirm the effective date of your address change? :eyes:

alex_m: DM sent a screenshot. Address change processed 2024-03-12. Last pay date was 2024-03-28.

payroll_bot: Automated notice: Payroll ticket #PR-4821 created for garnishment review. Please do not post PII in channel. :file_folder:

lenora_payroll: @alex_m thanks — I pulled the stub. Looks like a county levy from Multnomah County with a levy start date 2024-03-20. Even though you moved, levies follow the SSN until the agency issues a release. The 401(k) deferral decreased because garnishment is prioritized and reduced your net taxable wages for the pre-tax calculation in this pay period.

alex_m: I didn't get any notice from the county. Is there a path to get the withheld amount refunded or to restore the missed 401k deferral?

ben_legal: Short version: garnishments are controlled by the issuing agency/court. Next steps for you: 1) verify the levy with the county (they can confirm case number and amounts), 2) request a release or payoff statement, 3) provide release to payroll. Until payroll receives an official release, we must continue to honor the levy. Employer can't stop it unilaterally.

maria_hrbp: Looping in @tom_benefits to confirm if Fidelity can accept a manual catch-up contribution if payroll can't reapply the deferral this cycle.

tom_benefits: Fidelity supports corrective (after-the-fact) contributions in limited cases. We'll need a signed employee authorization and coordination from payroll to push a manual contribution. It also must fit within annual deferral limits.

lenora_payroll: Practical timeline/ops: once we have the release doc we can do a few things:
- Stop future garnishments: process change in next payroll cycle (typically 2–3 business days to action).
- For the $420 already withheld: if county issues a refund to employee, payroll can process a manual payroll adjustment or separate manual check depending on agency instructions. If the agency instructs employer to remit/return, we'll follow that.
- For 401(k): we can submit a corrective contribution request to Fidelity, but we need a signed authorization from you and payroll flagging the adjustment.

alex_m: If I get a release, what format does payroll need? PDF? court order?

ben_legal: PDF of the release or court order with case number and identifying info (usually full SSN or last 4) is standard. Do not post SSN in this channel — you can redact when sending here but payroll will need full data via secure channel.

people_ops: @alex_m use the secure HR upload: https://hr.redwood.com/upload (internal SSO). Do not send SSN in Slack. :lock: If you prefer, we can open a secure message thread and Lenora will follow up.

alex_m: Thanks. Also—will this force a W-2C or otherwise mess with my year end?

lenora_payroll: The garnishment itself doesn't change taxable wages reported on the W-2. However, if we process refunds or corrections after year-end (or reclassify amounts), that could trigger a W-2C. We'll flag the employee record for year-end review and document any adjustments.

maria_hrbp: We'll track this in the ticket. @lenora_payroll please note potential W-2C and benefits catch-up so it's on the year-end checklist.

lenora_payroll: Done — PR-4821 notes updated. ETA: initial payroll review within 2 business days. Correction/adjustment timeline depends on agency response; if we get a release this week we can aim to stop future withholdings in the next payroll and submit benefits corrective request immediately.

alex_m: Appreciate it. I'll contact Multnomah County today and DM any release. @ben_legal can you DM me that template for requesting release/proof?

ben_legal: Will DM a template and a short script you can use when calling the county. Also will include what to ask for to speed up release (case number, proof of payment or court date).

people_ops: Thanks everyone. Quick reminder: keep any sensitive docs in the secure upload so we can process promptly. :pray:

alex_m: Sending release via secure upload now. Will update here once I get confirmation from county.

lenora_payroll: Received uploaded doc. We’ll validate and update PR-4821 after matching. If valid, next payroll cycle we'll stop future garnishments and coordinate the benefits corrective with Fidelity.

payroll_bot: Update: PR-4821 status -> Investigating. Owner: lenora_payroll.

alex_m: Huge thanks — feeling less stressed. :smile:

maria_hrbp: We'll follow up with timeline in the ticket. If anything else pops up, DM me.

lenora_payroll: Keeping this open until agency confirms release and corrections processed. Closing note: employees sometimes need to follow up directly with the agency to request expedited release; we can help with documentation.
